feasibility_reasoning:
1. Three of the four hand sections are builder-widget CSS, not content-route CSS. Only key takeaways (rendered only in $.tsx) and .glossary-term are post-only.
- Footnotes (styles.css:8337-8666): src/components/builder/organisms/widget-view/RichHtmlContent.tsx:17-21,71 calls expandFootnotes and FootnoteTooltips. RichHtmlView is in the / chunk set, and ChromeWidgetView.tsx:808-810 also renders it in header/footer chrome on every route. BlocksRenderer.tsx:14-24,142 renders footnotes too.
- Code blocks (styles.css:3276-3406): rendered by BlocksRenderer, which the builder RichTextView.tsx:8,34 uses.
- Digital features (styles.css:4231-4341): FeatureWidgets.tsx:24-29 imports components/features/*.

2. There is no separable "content route". Posts render through the universal resolver src/routes/$.tsx:1-5, which also serves every CMS builder page; post.$slug.tsx:33-47 is only a 301. Builder content also renders in index.tsx, support.tsx, checkout.success.tsx, preview.$token.tsx, the events routes and SiteChrome. So content.css either goes back onto / (no gain), or footnotes, code blocks and features lose their styling on / and on the other builder routes. Importing it from the widgets instead makes it lazy-chunk CSS, which css.md §2.2 itself rules out for SSR-rendered React.lazy widgets (FOUC; CLS from sup font-size 0.5em arriving late).

3. The utility half cannot work as specified. tiers2.mjs already removes the content hand CSS in stage 1 and the content-only utilities in stage 2. Stage 3, which is what C6 is credited with, removes 902 utility rules / 79 KB raw in the ui-shadcn, builder-widgets, other and public-chrome areas. They are chosen by homeReach===false, which is runtime data: "candidate appears only in modules of the 79 chunks loaded in one fixture LH run" (analyze.mjs:31-35,105). A glob-based surfaceCssPlugin like adminCssPlugin.ts:5,26-33 cannot express that. Moving those candidates would leave interaction-gated UI on / unstyled (dialogs, popovers, login, search), plus builder widgets that are absent from the fixture home.

4. Gates and tests:
- chartClasses.test.ts:34 reads only styles.css and charts.css, so it breaks if the neh/feature rules move.
- The cssSurfaces test and the render-blocking gate line do not exist yet (they are C11).
- The publicCss sum (check-bundle-size.ts:2456-2461) rises with a split.
blocking_issues: Footnotes, code blocks and digital features are builder-widget CSS: RichHtmlContent.tsx:17-21,71 (via RichHtmlView, which loads on / and in ChromeWidgetView.tsx:808-810), RichTextView.tsx:8,34 -> BlocksRenderer, FeatureWidgets.tsx:24-29. Moving them to content routes breaks styling on / and on other builder routes, or reintroduces blocking or FOUC.

Posts and builder pages share the universal route src/routes/$.tsx. Builder content also renders in index, support, checkout.success, preview, events and SiteChrome, so no 'content route' import point exists that excludes / without regressions.

The stage-3 savings credited to C6 are not content utilities. They are 79 KB raw of ui-shadcn, builder-widgets, other and public-chrome utilities picked by runtime homeReach from one fixture run (analyze.mjs:31-35,105). A glob-based surfaceCssPlugin cannot express that, and moving them leaves lazy, interaction-gated UI on / unstyled.
chartClasses.test.ts:34 reads only styles.css and charts.css, so it fails if the digital-feature/neh rules move without updating it.
Depends on the cssSurfaces test and the render-blocking gate, which do not exist yet (C11). The publicCss sum rises with the split.
effect_reasoning:
The claimed effect (FCP -0.15 s, LCP -0.17 s) comes from the 'core' A/B: a 44.2 KB br sheet against the 70 KB br sheet of today. That is the whole surface split (C1 through C6) measured on the retired h1 harness, not C6's increment.

I re-simulated with the same rows.json and stage predicates (scratchpad verdicts/css-C6/sizes.mjs):
- Content hand CSS alone: -12.2 KB raw / -1.96 KB gzip-6 / -1.78 KB br.
- Key takeaways plus glossary only (the truly post-only part): -0.8 KB br.
- Honest C6 increment stacked on C1-C5, i.e. stage 2 without C6 versus stage 2 (hand plus content-only utilities): -28.6 KB raw / -3.8 KB gzip / -2.9 KB br.
- Stage 2 to stage 3 (credited to C6 but not content CSS): -7.4 KB br.

The lighthouse-analyst Lantern what-if says CSS -70 % (49 KB) gives FCP 0 because FCP is JS-bound, and LCP -225 ms, so about 4.6 ms per KB of the pre-LCP set. For 2.9 KB br that is LCP about -13 ms and FCP 0 to -15 ms. score.py at the 85 operating point (FCP and LCP 2800 to 2785 ms) gives 85.35 to 85.55, so about +0.1 to +0.2 mobile points and 0 on desktop. That is below the A/A noise of ±0.01 s, so measure-ab cannot confirm it. Even crediting the full 10.3 KB br from stage 2 to stage 3 gives only about -45 ms LCP, about +0.5 point.

I did not run a what-if: lighthouse-local only transforms HTML, swapping the sheet needs a patched artifact, and the delta is under the noise floor. The structural evidence decides.

Cheaper path: move only key takeaways and glossary-term into a CSS file imported by $.tsx (manifest route CSS, SSR-linked). C5 (color-mix strip, -5 KB gzip) and boot-js (hundreds of KB in the same pre-LCP set) give more for less risk.
corrected_estimate: Honest C6 (content hand CSS plus content-only utilities, stacked on C1-C5): -28.6 KB raw / -3.8 KB gzip-6 / -2.9 KB br render-blocking. At about 4.6 ms/KB that is mobile LCP about -13 ms and FCP 0 to -15 ms (JS-bound), about +0.1 to +0.2 mobile points and 0 desktop, not measurable at n=3. The safe subset (key takeaways and glossary-term via $.tsx route CSS) is -0.8 KB br, about -4 ms, about 0 points. The 'stage 3' figure (-7.4 KB br, about -35 to -45 ms) is not achievable by this mechanism without breaking shared UI.
better_alternative: Drop C6 as specified. Optionally move only key takeaways and .glossary-term into a stylesheet imported by src/routes/$.tsx (TanStack manifest route CSS, SSR-linked, no FOUC). Keep footnotes, code blocks and digital features in the core because they are builder-widget CSS. Do not build surfaceCssPlugin(content) for the stage-3 utilities. Spend the effort on C5 (color-mix fallback strip, -5 KB gzip on the whole sheet) and on boot-js preload cuts, which dominate the same pre-LCP set.
